questions.explanation: Positive agreement uses 'so + auxiliary + subject'.
Negative agreement uses 'neither + auxiliary + subject'.

questions.q: She said she'd help, and she ___.
questions.explanation: 'Do so' substitutes for a previously mentioned action.

options: He's tired, and so I am.
He's tired, and too am I.
He's tired, and so am I.
He's tired, and so do I.
questions.explanation: Positive agreement with 'be' uses 'so + am/is/are'.
Agreement with a negative uses 'neither'.
'Do so' avoids repeating the verb phrase.

options: She likes tea, and so her sister does.
She likes tea, and so does her sister too.
She likes tea, and her sister does so.
She likes tea, and so does her sister.
questions.explanation: Positive agreement uses 'so + auxiliary + subject'.
Negative agreement with 'will' uses 'neither will they'.

questions.q: He promised to call, but he never ___.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis after 'never' keeps just the auxiliary.

options: I don't eat meat, and neither my brother does.
I don't eat meat, and so doesn't my brother.
I don't eat meat, and neither does my brother.
I don't eat meat, and my brother doesn't neither.
questions.explanation: Negative agreement uses 'neither + auxiliary + subject'.
Positive agreement with 'be' uses 'so am I'.

questions.q: Take an umbrella if you think ___.
questions.explanation: 'Think so' substitutes for a whole clause.

options: They were exhausted, and so we were.
They were exhausted, and we were so.
They were exhausted, and so did we.
They were exhausted, and so were we.
questions.explanation: Agreement with past 'be' uses 'so + were'.
Negative agreement with the present perfect uses 'neither have I'.

questions.q: She asked him to leave, and he ___.
questions.explanation: 'Do so' refers back to the requested action.

options: He can speak French, and so can she.
He can speak French, and so she can.
He can speak French, and she can so.
He can speak French, and so does she.
questions.explanation: Agreement with a modal uses 'so + modal + subject'.
'I think so' avoids repeating the clause.

questions.q: They offered to help, but we didn't need them to ___.
questions.explanation: 'Do so' substitutes for the infinitive phrase.

options: I'm not ready, and neither is he.
I'm not ready, and neither he is.
I'm not ready, and so isn't he.
I'm not ready, and he isn't neither.
questions.explanation: Negative agreement uses 'neither + be + subject'.
'I hope not' substitutes for the negative clause.
